rulings.challenge_claim: The one-verse cut is tested only against the seam behind it while a two-verse-rare catchword and a shared frame-onset construction carry the verse across its own rear seam undisclosed; 'a further messenger formula, separately worded' understates a repeated onset construction.
rulings.grounds: The catchword item is byte-verified and load-bearing at this granularity; the onset-construction item needs narrowing. (a) UPHELD (byte + accent_stripped, cross-seam cohesion): חִנָּ֖ם (oshb:Isa.52.3, byte) recurs as חִנָּ֑ם (oshb:Isa.52.5, byte); each form is byte-unique to its own verse (sweep: 1 verse at byte each), the two match each other from accent_stripped tier down, and the token stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide, word-bound (sweep: 2 verses at accent_stripped and at word-bound skeleton -- oshb:Isa.52.3, oshb:Isa.52.5). The sold-for-nothing / taken-for-nothing pair therefore runs straight across this span's rear seam into the SECOND verse of the following unit, which argues 52:3-52:6 as one movement unless disclosed. Nothing in the row names it, and the rejected alternative tests only the seam behind the verse (folding back into the awake-Zion imperatives), leaving the seam the byte evidence actually contests untested. At a single-verse span that omission is the whole of the row's boundary argument on one side. (b) REFINED: the frames either side of the rear seam do share their construction -- כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר (oshb:Isa.52.3, byte) and כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ (oshb:Isa.52.4, byte), matching each other at SKELETON tier only (accent_stripped separates them) -- and the row does not name that. But 'separately worded' is not false: the titles genuinely differ, יְהוָ֔ה at oshb:Isa.52.3 against אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה at oshb:Isa.52.4. And the construction is not rare: the conjunction-plus-formula run stands at 14 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, so it is a shared onset shape worth disclosing, not a device that by itself contests the cut. OL's wording implies more force than the digit supports. Confirmed sound and not disturbed: the pointed splice reaches byte tier at its cited verse, the frame is divine (this book's royal-messenger sites are exactly oshb:Isa.36.4, oshb:Isa.36.14, oshb:Isa.36.16, oshb:Isa.37.3), the mark keyed to oshb:Isa.52.2 stands after that verse and so falls exactly at this span's front seam as the row reads it, and no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg falls in this one-verse span.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, row P14-019. (a) strongest_rejected_alternative: add the rear-seam rival -- holding oshb:Isa.52.3-52.6 as one movement -- and set it aside, or not, on the catchword evidence: name the object, its 2-verse word-bound book-wide site list and its accent_stripped tier, and note that the second site lies two verses past this cut. (b) boundary_rationale: keep 'separately worded' (the titles do differ, and name them) but add that both frames share the conjunction-plus-formula construction, with its tier (skeleton) and its 14-verse book-wide digit so the shared shape is not read as a rare tie. (c) When citing oshb:Isa.52.5 for the catchword, disclose that the verse carries TWO ketiv/qere notes (single-witness apparatus) and that the catchword token is not one of the variant tokens, so the splice is safe. TESTS: both seams of a single-verse span are tested in strongest_rejected_alternative; every digit names its object and whether it is word-bound; no recurrence claim ships without its tier. rulings.challenge_claim: The span's unit label rests entirely on the one verse the row never engages in the bytes, the English run standing in for that verse is not the translation's wording, and calling that verse both the structural center and a match to a recognized hymn-closure pattern is self-contradictory and unevidenced.
rulings.grounds: All three sub-claims verified; one piece of OL's own supporting evidence is refuted. (a) UPHELD (byte): the doxological label is carried by the sung imperatives at oshb:Isa.52.9 -- פִּצְח֤וּ רַנְּנוּ֙ -- and that two-token run is unique book-wide at every tier (sweep: 1 verse at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton). oshb:Isa.52.9 is the only verse of this span with no pointed splice anywhere in the row; the three that are spliced (oshb:Isa.52.7, oshb:Isa.52.8, oshb:Isa.52.10) are exclamation, report and announcement, not sung imperative. The label's actual byte warrant therefore goes unstated while an unquoted verse carries it. NEW FINDING sharpening this: that verse appears in NO evidence ref, either witness, although device_notes argues from it -- while every other verse the row argues is listed under both witnesses. This is an internal asymmetry rather than a mirror-rule failure, since the verse lies inside the row's own span, but it is the same omission showing twice. (b) UPHELD (translation bytes): the device note's English run is set in straight quotes and is not the translation's wording -- the source reads “Break out into joy! Sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem;” (web:Isa.52.9), with an exclamation point and initial capitals where the row has a comma and lower case. Straight quoting keeps a non-verbatim run of translation text out of reach of the verbatim arm inside a field that carries that verse's own web: ref. (c) UPHELD: naming one verse both the structural center of a four-verse span and a match to a recognised closure pattern is internally inconsistent, and neither characterisation carries evidence; the appeal to a recognised campaign pattern is also process framing rather than a textual signal. REFUTED, in OL's own supporting evidence: OL offers an arm-token 'attested in exactly 4 verses in the whole book (skeleton-tier sweep: 4 verses, MT 51:9, 52:10, 53:1, 63:12)'. That set is not reproducible under any consistent object. Taking זְר֣וֹעַ (oshb:Isa.52.10, byte) as the probe: word-bound skeleton gives 3 verses (oshb:Isa.51.9, oshb:Isa.52.10, oshb:Isa.63.12); prefix-tolerant word-bound gives 6 (adding oshb:Isa.44.12, oshb:Isa.53.1, oshb:Isa.62.8, all carrying the same prefixed form); the bare consonantal substring gives 8 and blends a DIFFERENT root at oshb:Isa.61.11, where the token is the sowing noun, not the arm. OL's 4 is the word-bound 3 plus oshb:Isa.53.1 while excluding the two other prefixed sites -- a hand-cut set, not a swept object. The herald participle digit is by contrast exact: מְבַשֵּׂ֗ר (oshb:Isa.52.7, byte) stands at 2 verses word-bound (oshb:Isa.41.27, oshb:Isa.52.7; byte 1 verse, accent_stripped 2, bare substring 4). Confirmed sound and not disturbed: the exclamatory onset is verse-initial, the following unit opens on a doubled imperative, the mark keyed to oshb:Isa.52.10 stands after that verse and so falls at this span's own close as the row reads it, and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, row P14-021. (a) boundary_rationale: splice the sung-imperative pair from oshb:Isa.52.9 at byte tier and state that it is the span's unit-label warrant, with its book-unique digit; add both witnesses' refs for that verse to boundary_evidence_refs so the row's citation practice is uniform across the four verses it argues. (b) device_notes: re-cut the translation run to the source wording in curly quotes with its web: ref in the same field, or drop the quotation and describe the call. (c) device_notes: delete the structural-center / recognised-pattern sentence and replace it with the byte fact -- the span's only sung-imperative pair -- or, if a positional claim is kept, make it one claim, not two incompatible ones. Do NOT import the 4-verse arm figure; if the arm chain is cited, name the object (word-bound 3, prefix-tolerant 6) and keep the sowing root out of it. rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row misstates its ordinary row-internal seam at web:Isa.52.12 as a frame boundary fixed at the parent-collection line, and its rejected alternative argues from assignment range rather than content. OL: the same, plus no byte evidence at all is offered at that seam while confidence is recorded high, and a one-sentence byte argument was available and unmade.
rulings.grounds: Both lenses land on ONE defect complex and the corpus confirms it outright; OL's additions are distinct and both hold. (1) FALSE STRUCTURAL CLAIM, both sources, UPHELD: the rationale calls this row's rear seam 'the frame boundary this campaign has fixed at the parent-collection line'. This row and the row that follows carry the IDENTICAL parent frame string spanning Isa.49.1-Isa.55.13; that frame runs from the row spanning Isa.49.1-Isa.49.6 to the row spanning Isa.55.6-Isa.55.13, and the frames on either side of it span Isa.40.1-Isa.48.22 and Isa.56.1-Isa.66.24. The nearest parent lines to this seam are therefore Isa.48.22|Isa.49.1 and Isa.55.13|Isa.56.1, and 52:12|52:13 sits well inside the frame. The claim asserts an architectural authority the row's own field denies. What the seam actually is, is a WRITER-PART change: this row and the next carry different writer-part values and the same parent. (2) VACUOUS RIVAL, both sources, UPHELD, with a rule neither primary named: strongest_rejected_alternative sets the extension aside 'because this row's own assigned range ends at web:Isa.52.12' and device_notes repeats the process framing. That is a workflow reason, not a textual one, so the one field designed to test the cut carries no evidence. NEW FINDING: it is also a REGISTER breach on its own terms -- assignment-range talk, part-boundary talk and campaign-process narration are barred from row prose in every field, independently of whether the reason is any good. (3) CONFIDENCE, OL only, UPHELD: confidence is recorded high while the only signal supplied at that seam is the mark keyed to oshb:Isa.52.12 (tier-3, single-witness, never a driver) -- and the neighbouring rows in this cluster, better evidenced, sit at medium. (4) AVAILABLE UNUSED BYTES, OL only, UPHELD: the next verse opens הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.52.13, byte; the three-token run unique at every tier) -- a presentative onset with a third-person verb and a first-person-suffixed servant noun -- against this span's second-person-plural departure imperatives ס֤וּרוּ ס֨וּרוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.52.11, byte; unique at every tier) and its escort promise הֹלֵ֤ךְ לִפְנֵיכֶם֙ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.52.12, byte). A one-sentence byte argument was there to be made and none was. Same defect or distinct: (1) and (2) are the same defect complex reached independently by both lenses -- the seam is justified by architecture and workflow rather than by text; (3) and (4) are OL-only and distinct, and together they turn a disclosure problem into an evidence vacuum at a seam held at the highest confidence in the cluster. Confirmed sound and not disturbed: the doubled onset imperative at oshb:Isa.52.11 reaches byte tier, the marks keyed to oshb:Isa.52.10 and oshb:Isa.52.12 are real and correctly read as closing after their keyed verses, and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span.

(b) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the workflow reason with a content reason argued from the bytes at the seam: the second-person-plural departure imperatives and escort promise of this span against the presentative third-person onset with its first-person-suffixed servant noun at the next verse, each spliced at byte tier with its tier named. rulings.challenge_claim: The rear seam is argued from a person-shift visible only in the translation, the same criterion cuts inside the span undisclosed, two byte-true hooks cross that seam without mention, and the onset is called a divine first-person oracle-opening formula that the rejected alternative then concedes is absent, with the servant noun filed under a divine-title signal class.
rulings.grounds: Three sub-claims upheld, one refined. (a) UPHELD (engagement class): the close is argued from a shift to a communal first-person-plural voice at the next verse, but no pointed form is quoted at oshb:Isa.52.15 or oshb:Isa.53.1 anywhere in the row -- the row's single Hebrew splice is its onset -- and neither verse appears under an oshb: ref. A boundary-relevant Hebrew form claim owes a pointed splice and a tier. In the bytes the shift is real -- לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte; unique at every tier) carries the first-person-plural suffix -- so the conclusion is byte-supportable; the defect is that it is carried entirely by the English rendering as written. (b) UPHELD and the strongest item: the row's own discriminator cuts INSIDE the span and is never named. oshb:Isa.52.13 speaks of the figure in the third person (עַבְדִּ֑י, with a third-person verb); oshb:Isa.52.14 addresses him in the second person masculine singular, עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ (byte; byte-unique to that verse), which the second witness renders as direct address; oshb:Isa.52.15 returns to the third person, עָלָ֛יו (byte). The rationale calls web:Isa.52.14-Isa.52.15 one continuous astonished-nations description. The internal shift is sharper than the one used to argue the close -- a second-person direct address against a third-to-first-plural voice change -- and applying the test at one seam while passing over it twice inside the span is the defect. (c) REFINED on both hooks: the arm hook is real but weaker and differently placed than OL says. וּזְר֥וֹעַ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte) against זְר֣וֹעַ קָדְשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.52.10, byte): collation of the oshb:Isa.52.10 token against oshb:Isa.53.1 reaches accent_stripped, the reverse returns none. OL's 'exactly 4 verses' is not reproducible under any consistent object -- word-bound skeleton gives 3 (oshb:Isa.51.9, oshb:Isa.52.10, oshb:Isa.63.12), prefix-tolerant word-bound gives 6 (adding oshb:Isa.44.12, oshb:Isa.53.1, oshb:Isa.62.8), and the bare substring gives 8 while blending the sowing root at oshb:Isa.61.11 -- and this is the SAME erratum OL carries in its P14-021 item. The hook also runs from a verse OUTSIDE this span to a verse one past its close, so it argues a motif chain across three rows, not against this row's own seam. The hearing hook is weaker still: שָׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.52.15, byte) and לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ collate to none against each other and share only a three-letter root as a consonantal substring, a substring that reaches 30 verses book-wide. Under the word-binding discipline that is a root-level echo, not a byte-true device, and it does not carry the continuity argument OL rests on it. Disclosure of both is worth a device note; neither contests the cut at the strength claimed. (d) UPHELD: the onset הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.52.13, byte) is called a divine first-person oracle-opening formula in the rationale while the rejected alternative concedes that no explicit frame formula marks a fresh oracle boundary here -- the row contradicts itself. The bytes support the concession, not the label: the presentative particle is verse-initial at 21 verses book-wide and present at 46, and it belongs to NONE of this book's frame-spine objects (not the messenger formula, not the woe-cry, not an oracle header, not the divine-speech signature); the verb is third-person; only the suffix on the servant noun is first-person. And the servant noun is then filed under a divine-title signal class, which misassigns it -- this book's divine-title objects are the tetragrammaton, adonai, the of-hosts title, the Holy-One-of-Israel title and the short form; עַבְדִּ֑י is the servant designation with a first-person suffix, a servant-census object (23 verses), and the row already carries two correct servant keys. Confirmed sound and not disturbed: the single pointed splice reaches byte tier at its cited verse, no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg falls in oshb:Isa.52.13-52.15, the inventory records no mark interior to the span, no messenger or narrator frame interrupts it, and the referent is properly left undecided.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, row P15-001. (a) boundary_rationale: splice the first-person-plural form at oshb:Isa.53.1 and a third-person form at oshb:Isa.52.15 at byte tier, with tiers named, and add both under oshb: refs, so the close-seam argument stands on pointed text rather than on the translation. (b) boundary_rationale: name the internal person shift across oshb:Isa.52.13, oshb:Isa.52.14 and oshb:Isa.52.15 with its spliced forms, and state why it does not cut the span even though the same class of shift is used to end it -- or record that it is a live internal seam. (c) Replace the onset label: describe what stands there -- a presentative particle, a third-person verb, and a first-person suffix on the servant noun -- and drop 'divine first-person oracle-opening formula', which the row's own rejected alternative already concedes away. (d) observed_substrate_signals: move the servant noun out of the divine-title family into the servant family; the divine-title keys are for the divine-name objects only. (e) device_notes: disclose the arm-noun chain and the hearing echo at their honest tiers and with a named object (word-bound 3 or prefix-tolerant 6 for the arm; root-level substring for the hearing echo), and state that both reach outside this span rather than contesting its seam. (f) Cite the front-seam mark under an oshb: ref with its type and single-witness label, as the neighbouring rows do; the parashah layer is Masoretic-keyed even where the chapter is identity-numbered. TESTS the cure must pass: every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim in the row has a pointed splice and a tier; the discriminator used at the close is applied, or expressly declined, at every place inside the span where it recurs; no field labels the onset with a frame-formula class the frame spine does not carry; no signal key files a servant object under a divine-title family. NOT AUTHOR WORK: cutting the span at the internal person shift, or moving the close, is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption, and the servant referent stays undecided in every repair.
